SASRec scores training positives/negatives with per-position embedding dot products and inference candidates using the final sequence feature. A transition residual therefore needs explicit recent-item context alongside features: `score(features, context_ids, candidate_ids)`. Proposed implementation: flatten valid B×L positions, broadcast candidate IDs, and add `λ Σ_r w_r A[context_r, candidate]`, where A contains transitions computed exclusively from training histories. Store sorted CSR rows; implement candidate lookup through vectorized edge-key search or padded neighbor tables. This interface recommendation follows the scoring structure in the [original SASRec implementation](https://github.com/kang205/SASRec/blob/master/model.py).

PyTorch supports CSR/COO sparse multiplication through [torch.sparse.mm](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.sparse.mm.html). [sampled_addmm](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.sparse.sampled_addmm.html) computes dense dot products at CSR-selected locations; it does not directly solve arbitrary transition-edge lookup. Implementation assessment: moderate difficulty, principally context plumbing and identical scoring across paths. For full-catalog recommendations, compute dense SASRec scores in item chunks, accumulate matching transition contributions, mask padding/seen items, and merge chunk top-k results. Preserve parity by sharing residual weights, normalization, context extraction and scoring code between training, validation and the generated predictor; serialize graph buffers and configuration. Verify candidate scores against corresponding full-catalog entries. No measured speedup or recommendation-quality gain is established by these sources.
